title: Phase 1: Scaffold workflow_dispatch skeleton + core Java build
description:
Create .github/workflows/release-preflight.yml — the minimal "Run workflow" button that builds the Java core and produces a summary.

**Files:** .github/workflows/release-preflight.yml (create)

**Context:**
- Model on build-test.yml triggers/setup. workflow_dispatch with inputs appears as a "Run workflow" button.
- Core build mirrors doc step 5a: mvn clean install. Use temurin JDK 11, cache: maven.
- Reuse EXCLUDE_MODULES/EXCLUDE_FOR_GLV env vars from build-test.yml so Java-only build excludes GLVs.
- Add a summary job that aggregates results and writes a pre-flight checklist to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY.

**Steps:**
1. Create workflow with: name "Release Pre-Flight Check"; on workflow_dispatch with inputs: version (string, required), deploy_snapshot (boolean, default false), publish_docs (boolean, default false). permissions: contents: read. Concurrency group.
2. Copy env block (EXCLUDE_MODULES, EXCLUDE_FOR_GLV) from build-test.yml.
3. Add job core-build (ubuntu-latest, ~45m): checkout@v6 → setup-java@v5 (temurin, 11, cache: maven) → mvn clean install -pl $EXCLUDE_MODULES -q -Dci.
4. Add job summary (needs: all jobs, if: always()) that prints each job result and manual checklist to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY.

**Test command:** Manually trigger from Actions tab. Locally lint with actionlint or validate YAML: python -c "import yaml,sys; yaml.safe_load(open(path))".

title: Phase 0: Prerequisite — remove mono from .NET packaging (TINKERPOP-2085)
description:
Remove the mono dependency from the .NET template packaging step so the pre-flight dotnet-template job runs cleanly on GitHub-hosted runners without mono.

**Files:** gremlin-dotnet/src/pom.xml (edit), docker/Dockerfile (edit), docs/src/dev/developer/release.asciidoc (edit if commands change)

**Context:**
- The only mono usage is the Ant exec at gremlin-dotnet/src/pom.xml:269 inside the glv-dotnet-deploy profile (activated by -Dnuget): package phase runs "mono ${nugetExe} pack Gremlin.Net.Template/Gremlin.Net.Template.nuspec" (downloads nuget.exe from dist.nuget.org first); deploy phase runs "mono ${nugetExe} push ..." for publishing.
- mono-devel is installed in docker/Dockerfile:33 solely for this.
- Replacement: dotnet pack -p:NuspecFile=Gremlin.Net.Template/Gremlin.Net.Template.nuspec -o <out> and dotnet nuget push. Both cross-platform, available wherever setup-dotnet runs.
- Tracked by TINKERPOP-2085.

**Steps:**
1. In gremlin-dotnet/src/pom.xml, replace the pack-dotnet-template execution mono exec with dotnet pack against the nuspec (drop the "available file=mono" guard and wget nuget.exe download). Verify produced .nupkg matches todays output.
2. Replace deploy-nuget execution mono push with dotnet nuget push.
3. Remove mono-devel (and mono apt repo lines, docker/Dockerfile:29) from the build container.
4. Update release.asciidoc if documented command text changes (-Dnuget invocation stays the same).

**Test command:** touch gremlin-dotnet/src/.glv gremlin-dotnet/test/.glv && mvn clean install -pl :gremlin-dotnet-source -Dnuget -am -Dci -DskipTests on a clean machine WITHOUT mono installed; confirm .nupkg produced under gremlin-dotnet/src/target.

title: Phase 5: License/NOTICE (RAT) + javadoc generation + upgrade-prompt existence (doc steps 5f, 5g, 6)
description:
Add a static-checks job for license-header validation (RAT), javadoc build verification, and upgrade-prompt existence check.

**Files:** .github/workflows/release-preflight.yml (edit)

**Context:**
- apache-rat-plugin configured at pom.xml:463 — mvn apache-rat:check flags missing/incorrect license headers (partial coverage of step 5f; LICENSE/NOTICE content review stays manual).
- Step 5g: build javadoc to confirm it generates without error. The ci profile skips javadoc, so run WITHOUT -Dci: mvn -q -DskipTests javadoc:javadoc (at minimum on gremlin-core).
- Step 6: assert docs/upgrade/prompts/upgrade-<version>-helper.md exists for the dispatched version. Currently only upgrade-3.8.0-helper.md exists; this is an existence check that fails soft (warning) — content validity remains a human task.

**Steps:**
1. Add job static-checks (needs core-build):
   - mvn apache-rat:check -q (fail the job on RAT violations — these are objective).
   - mvn -q -DskipTests -pl gremlin-core javadoc:javadoc to confirm javadoc generates.
   - Shell check: test -f docs/upgrade/prompts/upgrade-${{ inputs.version }}-helper.md → write ::warning:: and add to summary if missing (do not hard-fail).

**Test command:** Trigger workflow; confirm RAT runs, javadoc generates, prompt-existence result reported.

title: Release Pre-Flight Check Automation
description: Encode the entire pre-flight check from docs/src/dev/developer/release.asciidoc into a single workflow_dispatch GitHub Actions button at .github/workflows/release-preflight.yml. Heavy non-side-effecting verification (integration tests, docs generation, dependency reports) runs on every press. Only genuinely side-effecting steps (SNAPSHOT deploy to Apache Nexus, docs publish to SVN) are gated behind explicit opt-in inputs (default OFF). Human/comms items (mailing-list emails, LICENSE/NOTICE sign-off, JIRA hygiene review) are assisted via generated email drafts and decision-support data gathered by the workflow. Feasibility verdict: FEASIBLE — the mechanical/verification core is fully automatable; communication steps and final human sign-offs cannot be automated but the workflow pre-populates drafts and gathers supporting data so the human action is reduced to read/sanity-check/copy-paste-send. One prerequisite: remove mono from .NET packaging (TINKERPOP-2085).

title: Phase 9: Aggregate pre-flight report + manual checklist
description:
Complete the summary job (stubbed in Phase 1) so a single run produces a clear pass/fail dashboard, links the Phase 8 human-assist artifacts, and lists the residual non-automatable checklist.

**Files:** .github/workflows/release-preflight.yml (edit)

**Context:**
- The summary job (needs: every job including Phase 8 jobs, if: always()) reads each job result via needs.<job>.result and renders a markdown table to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY.
- Appends a "Manual checklist — needs human judgment" section: step 1 (language-runtime upgrades), final LICENSE/NOTICE sign-off (link to dependency-change report), javadoc-filter review, JIRA-hygiene confirmation (link report), upgrade-prompt content review, and "send the drafted T-14 / T-7 emails" (link drafts) — each as unchecked task.
- Optionally fail overall run only if hard-required jobs (core-build, static-checks) failed; assistive/optional jobs report status without failing the button.

**Steps:**
1. In summary (needs: every job, if: always()), read each job result and render markdown table to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY.
2. Append "Manual checklist — needs human judgment" section with unchecked tasks and links to human-assist artifacts.
3. Fail overall run only if core-build or static-checks failed.

**Test command:** Trigger workflow; confirm run summary shows dashboard, links to human-assist artifacts, and the checklist.

title: Phase 3: Docker-image build + Gremlin.Net.Template packaging (doc steps 5c, 5d)
description:
Add jobs to build Docker images (gremlin-server, gremlin-console) and validate Gremlin.Net.Template .nupkg packaging — both non-side-effecting (no push/publish at install phase).

**Files:** .github/workflows/release-preflight.yml (edit)

**Context:**
- Step 5c: mvn clean install -pl gremlin-server,gremlin-console -DdockerImages. The docker-images profile (fabric8) only docker:pushes at deploy phase, so install builds images locally — safe.
- Step 5d: mvn clean install -pl :gremlin-dotnet-source -Dnuget validates template packages. After Phase 0, glv-dotnet-deploy profile uses dotnet pack (no mono). Just install .NET SDK via setup-dotnet and create .glv sentinels.
- Both depend on core artifacts from Phase 1 core-build (resolve from ~/.m2 cache or rebuild with -am).

**Steps:**
1. Add job docker-images (needs core-build): checkout, setup-java (cache maven), mvn clean install -pl gremlin-server,gremlin-console -DdockerImages -Dci -DskipTests. Confirm images via docker images | grep tinkerpop.
2. Add job dotnet-template (needs core-build, needs Phase 0 landed): setup-java + setup-dotnet@v5 (8.0.x); touch gremlin-dotnet/src/.glv gremlin-dotnet/test/.glv; mvn clean install -pl :gremlin-dotnet-source -Dnuget -am -Dci -DskipTests. Verify .nupkg produced under gremlin-dotnet/src/target.

**Test command:** Trigger workflow; confirm both jobs green, image and nupkg presence logged.

title: Phase 2: Dependency-update report (doc step 3)
description:
Add a dependency-report job that runs on every press (non-gated, non-failing) and surfaces available minor/patch updates across all ecosystem toolchains.

**Files:** .github/workflows/release-preflight.yml (edit)

**Context:**
- Doc step 3 lists four tools: mvn versions:display-dependency-updates -DallowMajorUpdates=false, go list -m -u all, npm-check-updates, dotnet-check-updates.
- Needs setup-java (mvn), setup-go (Go 1.25, gremlin-go/), setup-node (npm-check-updates in gremlin-js/), setup-dotnet (8.0.x, dotnet-outdated-tool).
- Report only — never fails the run on available updates. Capture stdout to files, append to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY, upload as artifact.

**Steps:**
1. Add job dependency-report (runs on every press; no gate).
2. Run each tool redirecting output to reports/deps-*.txt. go list -m -u all in gremlin-go/; npx npm-check-updates in gremlin-js/; dotnet outdated in gremlin-dotnet/src.
3. actions/upload-artifact@v7 the reports/ directory; append summarized contents to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY.
4. Set continue-on-error: true on tool steps so a hiccup does not fail pre-flight.

**Test command:** Trigger workflow; confirm artifact dependency-report and a summary section appear.

title: Phase 8: Human-assist — decision-support data + pre-populated email drafts (doc steps 2, 4, 5f, 5h, 6)
description:
Add jobs that gather decision-support data and pre-populate email drafts for the human/comms steps that cannot be fully automated.

**Files:** .github/workflows/release-preflight.yml (edit); optionally bin/preflight-emails.sh (new helper) and email-draft templates

**Context:**
Two kinds of assist:
1. Decision-support data:
   - JIRA hygiene (5h): run three queries from the doc against JIRA REST API for dispatched version — (a) tickets with no Component, (b) tickets not type Bug/Improvement, (c) Resolved not Closed, (d) no Fix Version but marked Fixed/Done. Render as table. Needs JIRA_TOKEN secret; if absent, emit ::warning:: and skip.
   - LICENSE/NOTICE change data (5f): generate dependency-tree delta vs. last release tag (mvn dependency:tree diff) showing added/removed/bumped dependencies.
   - Upgrade-prompt status (6): report existence, last-modified date, git log of upgrade prompt file.
2. Pre-populated email drafts (2, 4):
   - T-14 reminder to dev list (note open issues, request upgrade-doc + CHANGELOG review).
   - T-7 code-freeze announcement.
   Generate ready-to-send text with version filled in and open-issue list embedded for copy/paste.

**Steps:**
1. Add job jira-hygiene (runs if JIRA_TOKEN present): query four conditions via JIRA REST, write reports/jira-hygiene.md, upload artifact, append to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY. Soft-fail if token missing.
2. Add job license-diff (needs core-build): compute dependency-tree delta vs. previous release tag; write reports/dependency-changes.md + upload artifact.
3. Add step (in summary or dedicated email-drafts job) rendering T-14 and T-7 email drafts to reports/email-*.md (and into job summary in fenced code blocks for one-click copy), interpolating version and open-issue list.
4. Keep all non-failing — assistive, not gates.

**Test command:** Trigger workflow; confirm JIRA table (or token-missing warning), dependency-change report artifact, and two copy-pasteable email drafts all appear in run summary/artifacts.

title: Phase 6: Documentation generation validation (doc step 7, non-publishing) — heavy, runs every press
description:
Add a docs-validation job that runs bin/process-docs.sh (generation only, no SVN publish). Non-side-effecting, runs on every press per the exhaustive pre-flight rationale.

**Files:** .github/workflows/release-preflight.yml (edit)

**Context:**
- Step 7 ultimately runs bin/publish-docs.sh (publishes to SVN). The validation value is confirming doc generation succeeds — run bin/process-docs.sh without publishing.
- process-docs.sh needs a built project, Python 3, Groovy, netcat, and starts bin/gephi-mock.py on port 8080. It executes live Gremlin examples (slow, can be flaky).
- Generation is non-side-effecting; only the SVN publish (Phase 7b) is gated.

**Steps:**
1. Add job docs-validation (runs on every press), timeout-minutes: 120, needs core-build.
2. setup-java + setup-python@v6 + install Groovy + netcat; mvn clean install -DskipTests -q (build first, doc requires built console); then chmod +x bin/process-docs.sh && bin/process-docs.sh (generation only — confirm -d/--dryRun semantics against the script).
3. Upload generated HTML under target/ (or docs output dir) as an artifact for manual eyeballing (doc stresses visually checking for gray code blocks).

**Test command:** Trigger workflow; confirm docs generate and artifact uploads.

title: Phase 4: Full integration test suite (doc step 5b) — heavy, runs every press
description:
Add the full dockerized integration test suite job. Runs on every press (not gated) per the exhaustive pre-flight rationale — pre-flight runs rarely and every verification step is necessary.

**Files:** .github/workflows/release-preflight.yml (edit)

**Context:**
- Step 5b: docker/build.sh -t -i. Builds base images and runs the full integration suite across GLVs via docker compose. Long-running (can exceed 1 hour). GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest has Docker + compose available.
- The script bind-mounts ~/.m2, gremlin-server, gremlin-test, gremlin-console. Calls docker/build-containers.sh -h <HADOOP_VERSION> first.
- Not gated — slow background run is acceptable for infrequent pre-flight. Give generous timeout.

**Steps:**
1. Add job integration-tests (runs on every press), timeout-minutes: 180.
2. checkout@v6 → setup-java@v5 (11, cache maven) → chmod +x docker/build.sh → docker/build.sh -t -i.
3. On failure, actions/upload-artifact@v7 any **/target/surefire-reports and container logs.

**Test command:** Trigger workflow (expect >1h run). For faster iteration during development, first validate job definition with a no-op echo before wiring the real script.

title: Phase 7: Side-effecting stages — SNAPSHOT deploy + docs publish (gated + secrets) [HIGH-RISK]
description:
⚠️ HIGH-RISK / SIDE-EFFECTING. These push to shared Apache infrastructure. Default OFF. Require secrets and explicit input toggles.

Add gated jobs for SNAPSHOT deploy (5e) and docs publish (7). Follow Log4j secret-injection pattern (setup-java server-id/server-username/server-password, gpg-private-key; svn non-interactive).

**Files:** .github/workflows/release-preflight.yml (edit); repo secrets configured in GitHub UI

**Context:**
- 5e SNAPSHOT deploy: mvn clean deploy pushes to https://repository.apache.org/snapshots/. Needs Apache Nexus creds. For pre-flight, deploying the Java SNAPSHOT is the documented action.
- 7 docs publish: bin/publish-docs.sh <username> commits to ASF SVN. Must be made non-interactive (currently prompts for SVN password) — pass creds via env/args with --username/--password --non-interactive.
- These are gated behind inputs.deploy_snapshot and inputs.publish_docs (both default false).

**Steps:**
1. Add job deploy-snapshot gated by if: inputs.deploy_snapshot. Configure setup-java with server-id for Apache snapshots and NEXUS_USERNAME/NEXUS_PASSWORD secrets; run mvn clean deploy -DskipTests -Dci.
2. Add job publish-docs gated by if: inputs.publish_docs requiring SVN_USERNAME/SVN_PASSWORD secrets. Prerequisite code change: make bin/publish-docs.sh accept non-interactive password (env var SVN_PASSWORD) instead of prompting. Then invoke from the job.
3. Add environment-protection rule (GitHub environment: with required reviewers) on these two jobs.

**Test command:** Do NOT test against production Apache infra. Validate job wiring with act or dry-run flag; require explicit maintainer review before first real use.
